the duration of epileptiform activity in electrically stunned sheep is dependent upon excitant amino acid receptor activation.

the development of an epileptiform-like condition following an electric stun of the head in sheep is dependent on excitatory amino acid (EAA) receptors, and that the reflex suppression that also occurs following an electric stun in sheep is dependent, in part, on GABAergic receptor mechanisms.
the duration of epileptiform activity following an electric head stun is reduced by excitatory amino acid receptor blockers and increased by a GABA receptor blocker.

the development of an alternative method of humane stunning for sheep.
the development of new anesthetic techniques for the humane stunning of livestock and the development of new methods of stunning for the humane slaughter of livestock.
